statute: Directive 2001/83/EC as amended by Directive 2004/24/EC; European Medicines Agency (HMPC)
section_rule: Traditional use registration and food route
title: European Union: Traditional Herbal Medicinal Products Directive 2004/24/EC and food-supplement rules
content:
Export of an Ayurvedic herbal product to the European Union generally follows one of several routes depending on how the product is presented and what is claimed.

1. Traditional herbal medicinal product registration: the simplified traditional-use registration procedure requires evidence of traditional use over a long period, including a period within the EU, plus quality and safety documentation. Products relying on non-EU traditional use alone may face difficulty meeting the usage-period condition.
2. Food or food-supplement route: products presented without medicinal claims may be marketed as food supplements under food law, subject to rules on permitted ingredients, novel foods, health claims and contaminant limits.
3. Quality expectations: authorities look closely at heavy-metal and contaminant limits and at proper identification of botanical ingredients.
4. Practical link: the regulatory route must be chosen before labelling and claims are finalised, and a local regulatory representative or importer of record is typically involved.

This is a short curated summary for orientation, not the directive text. Requirements differ by member state; check the competent authority before export.
